model_organism.citation: Motor coordination and behavioural deficits in a mouse model of KMT2B-related dystonia (PMID: 42727616)
phenotypes: Viable but significantly smaller and lighter than littermate controls
Hyperlocomotion in the open field
About two-fold larger acoustic startle responses
Enhanced prepulse inhibition at all prepulse intensities
Slower balance beam crossing with more pauses
Female knockouts paused more on the ladder rung task
Claw-like hindpaw posture with abnormal inward flexion of the digits (dystonic-like)
Reduced investigation of a novel conspecific (reduced sociability) with intact social recognition memory
Striatal Kmt2b transcript reduced to about half of control levels
177 differentially expressed genes in striatum, including Maob, implicating neurodevelopmental, glial and mitochondrial processes
Nociception, vision, body-weight-adjusted grip strength, clinical chemistry and haematology largely unaffected

Deficit in H3K4 di- and trimethylation at downregulated plasticity genes, with H3K4me1 unaffected

phenotypes: Mll2 CKO in Chx10+ retinal progenitors gave a phenotype similar to Mll1 CKO

Thin retinal layers and shorter photoreceptor outer segments with impaired phototransduction gene expression
Reduced numbers of M-cones, horizontal cells and amacrine neurons, followed by fast retinal degeneration
Moderately reduced progenitor proliferation at P0
Increased apoptosis and reactive gliosis postnatally
Removal of both MLLs in rods gave a normal phenotype, while the M-cone CKO impaired M-cone function and survival

biological.citation: Structure, Activity and Function of the MLL2 (KMT2B) Protein Lysine Methyltransferase (PMID: 34440566)
biological.summary: Review describing KMT2B (MLL2) as a 2715-aa H3K4 methyltransferase with a C-terminal SET domain. It forms a complex with WRAD (WDR5, RbBP5, ASH2L, DPY30), HCF1/2 and Menin, and the complex deposits H3K4me3 at promoters and cis-regulatory sites of bivalent developmental genes. The review also notes wide expression in adult human tissues.

biological.citation: Regulation, functions and transmission of bivalent chromatin during mammalian development (PMID: 36028557)
biological.summary: Review identifying KMT2B, together with PRC2, as a key factor establishing bivalent chromatin (H3K4me3/H3K27me3) at developmental gene promoters. Bivalency is a feature of germline and embryonic stem cells and is relevant to development and cancer.

biological.citation: H3K4me1 facilitates promoter-enhancer interactions and gene activation during embryonic stem cell differentiation (PMID: 38513661)
biological.summary: In mouse ESCs undergoing neural differentiation, H3K4me1 at KMT2C/D-independent enhancers was reduced after acute KMT2B depletion, which aggravated transcriptional defects. This implicates KMT2B in catalyzing H3K4me1 at enhancers and supports a role for H3K4me1 in enhancer-promoter interactions.

biological.citation: KMT2A and KMT2B Mediate Memory Function by Affecting Distinct Genomic Regions (PMID: 28723559)
biological.summary: Knockdown of Kmt2b in mouse hippocampal neurons decreased H3K4 methylation and deregulated gene expression, and it impaired memory. Kmt2b and Kmt2a control largely distinct genomic regions and molecular pathways linked to neuronal plasticity.

biological.citation: Tsga8 is required for spermatid morphogenesis and male fertility in mice (PMID: 33766931)
biological.summary: KMT2B deposits H3K4me3 at bivalent and monovalent promoters in undifferentiated spermatogonia and programs genes for later expression. Tsga8 is one such KMT2B target, and its loss in mice causes male infertility through defective spermatid morphogenesis and histone-to-protamine transition.

biological.citation: KMT2B promotes the growth of renal cell carcinoma via upregulation of SNHG12 expression and promotion of CEP55 transcription (PMID: 35597996)
biological.summary: In RCC cells, KMT2B upregulated lncRNA SNHG12 by increasing H3K4me3 at its promoter (ChIP). SNHG12 then recruited E2F1 to drive CEP55 transcription, promoting proliferation, migration, invasion and angiogenesis in vitro and tumor growth in nude mouse xenografts.

biological.citation: Haploinsufficiency of KMT2B, Encoding the Lysine-Specific Histone Methyltransferase 2B, Results in Early-Onset Generalized Dystonia (PMID: 27839873)
biological.summary: Four loss-of-function KMT2B mutations (three de novo, one inherited) were identified in early-onset generalized dystonia. Mutant patient fibroblasts showed significantly decreased KMT2B mRNA, consistent with haploinsufficiency and disordered histone modification as a disease mechanism.
biological.significance: significantly decreased mRNA levels in mutant fibroblasts

biological.citation: Genetic landscape of non-UV-induced cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas (PMID: 41132030)
biological.summary: KMT2B carried high-impact loss-of-function mutations in 11/31 non-UV-induced cSCC, a significantly higher proportion than in UV-induced cSCC. siRNA knockdown of KMT2B in SCC-13 and A-431 cells did not change proliferation but significantly increased migration.
biological.significance: significantly higher mutation frequency than UV-induced cSCC; significantly increased migration

biological.summary: Rare heterozygous KMT2B missense variants were found in adult-onset dystonia, hearing loss or intellectual disability. Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling separated these cases from controls and from early-onset DYT-KMT2B patients, indicating a distinct epigenetic signature.

biological.citation: Phenotype variability and allelic heterogeneity in KMT2B-Associated disease (PMID: 29653907)
biological.summary: Four novel de novo KMT2B frameshift/insertion mutations were identified in Japanese dystonia patients, and the mutant transcripts showed reduced mRNA expression. This supports haploinsufficiency as a pathomechanism, with cerebellar involvement noted.
